items.name: Combat Basics
items.description: Pokémon 5e uses D&D 5e combat with additional rules for Trainers and their Pokémon.

details.label: Initiative
details.value: Roll initiative separately for each Pokémon in battle; the Trainer acts with their first Pokémon.

details.label: Commands
details.value: As an action, a Trainer may issue up to two commands, with no more than one command for each Pokémon.

details.label: Many active Pokémon
details.value: With three or more Pokémon active, commands may be issued to two; the others may move only.

items.name: Move Power
items.description: Move Power determines the ability modifier used for a Move's attack, damage, and saving throw calculations.

details.label: Attack bonus
details.value: Move Power modifier + Proficiency bonus

details.label: Damage bonus
details.value: Move Power modifier + STAB

details.label: Save DC
details.value: 8 + Move Power modifier + Proficiency bonus

details.label: Multiple powers
details.value: Choose one listed Move Power when a Move offers more than one.

items.name: Same-Type Attack Bonus (STAB)
items.description: A Pokémon gains STAB when its Move shares one of its types.

details.label: Bonus
details.value: Add the Pokémon's Proficiency bonus to damage.

details.label: Limit
details.value: STAB cannot be negative and is added only once per Move per target.

items.name: Switching Pokémon
items.description: Trainers may recall and release Pokémon as an action; switching a fainted Pokémon may be a reaction.

details.label: Action switch
details.value: Recall up to two Pokémon within 60 feet and release replacements within 15 feet and line of sight.

details.label: Fainted switch
details.value: A fainted Pokémon can be switched immediately as a reaction, out of turn.

details.label: After switching in
details.value: A switched-in Pokémon cannot move or take actions, reactions, or bonus actions this round unless it starts a new round.

details.label: Poké Ball
details.value: Concentration and Move or item buffs end when a Pokémon returns; status conditions remain.

items.name: Flying, Hovering, and Burrowing
items.description: Special movement changes how Pokémon target, fall, and travel across the battlefield.

details.label: Ranged attacks in flight
details.value: Beyond half range, ranged attack rolls have disadvantage; targets have advantage on saving throws.

details.label: Falling
details.value: A flying Pokémon falls when its flight speed becomes zero; a hovering Pokémon falls without fall damage.

details.label: Burrowing
details.value: Burrowing just below suitable ground remains targetable. Deeper burrowing is difficult terrain and leaves a difficult-terrain tunnel.

items.name: Raised and Grounded
items.description: Some Moves affect Raised and Grounded creatures differently.

details.label: Raised
details.value: A creature using fly or hover speed, with Levitate, an Air Balloon, Magnet Rise, or Telekinesis.

details.label: Grounded
details.value: A creature not using fly or hover speed, or one that is prone or has its fly or hover speed reduced to zero.

items.name: Opportunity Attacks and Readying
items.description: Pokémon can react to a foe leaving melee range or prepare a Move for a trigger.

details.label: Opportunity attack
details.value: Leaving melee range without Disengage allows a reaction using a 1-action melee Move; it costs its normal PP.

details.label: Readied Move
details.value: Choose the Move, spend PP, and define a trigger. Readying requires concentration; losing it loses the PP.

items.name: Status Conditions Overview
items.description: A Pokémon may have one non-volatile and one volatile status condition at the same time.

details.label: Non-volatile
details.value: A Pokémon cannot gain another non-volatile condition until its current one is cured.

details.label: Volatile
details.value: Volatile conditions end outside combat or when the Pokémon is switched out.

details.label: Grace period
details.value: After recovering, a Pokémon cannot receive the same condition until after the end of its next turn.

items.name: Asleep
items.description: The Pokémon is incapacitated and restrained for up to three rounds.

details.label: Saving throws
details.value: All saving throws are made with disadvantage.

details.label: Recovery
details.value: At the end of each turn or after forced movement, roll a d20; on 11 or higher, the condition ends.

items.name: Burned
items.description: Burned Pokémon suffer weaker damage rolls and ongoing damage.

details.label: Damage rolls
details.value: Roll each damage roll twice and use the lower result.

details.label: Ongoing damage
details.value: Take damage equal to Proficiency bonus at the end of each turn until cured or unconscious.

details.label: Immunity
details.value: Fire-type Pokémon are immune.

items.name: Frozen
items.description: Frozen Pokémon are incapacitated and restrained until they break free or are thawed.

details.label: Duration
details.value: Lasts up to one hour.

details.label: Recovery
details.value: At the end of a turn, make a Strength save against DC 10 + the source's Proficiency bonus; fire damage can also end it.

details.label: Immunity
details.value: Ice-type Pokémon are immune.

items.name: Paralysis
items.description: Paralysis impairs movement and can briefly incapacitate a Pokémon.

details.label: Penalties
details.value: Strength and Dexterity saving throws have disadvantage; speed is halved.

details.label: Turn check
details.value: At the start of each turn, roll a d4. On 1, the Pokémon is incapacitated and restrained until its next turn.

details.label: Immunity
details.value: Electric-type Pokémon are immune.

items.name: Poisoned
items.description: Poisoned Pokémon have reduced effectiveness and take ongoing damage.

details.label: Penalties
details.value: Ability checks and attack rolls have disadvantage.

details.label: Ongoing damage
details.value: Take damage equal to Proficiency bonus at the end of each turn until cured or unconscious.

details.label: Immunity
details.value: Poison- and Steel-type Pokémon are immune.

items.name: Badly Poisoned
items.description: Badly Poisoned is a stronger form of Poisoned.

details.label: Penalties
details.value: Ability checks and attack rolls have disadvantage.

details.label: Ongoing damage
details.value: Take damage equal to twice Proficiency bonus at the end of each turn until cured or unconscious.

details.label: Immunity
details.value: Poison- and Steel-type Pokémon are immune.

items.name: Confused
items.description: Confused Pokémon cannot take reactions and roll a d8 at the start of each turn.

details.value: Use Struggle against itself or the nearest valid Pokémon target.
Cannot move or take actions.
Choose its behavior normally.
The condition ends.

items.name: Flinched
items.description: Flinched Pokémon are less effective until the end of their next turn.

details.label: Penalties
details.value: Attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws have disadvantage.

details.label: Saving throw Moves
details.value: Targets have advantage on a saving throw caused by the Flinched Pokémon's action.

items.name: Catching Pokémon
items.description: Use the Throw Pokéball action to attempt a capture of an eligible wild Pokémon.

details.label: Check
details.value: Make an Animal Handling check against the capture DC; several status conditions grant advantage.

details.label: Base DC
details.value: 10 + the Pokémon's Species Rating rounded down + its level.

details.label: Health
details.value: Reduce the DC by 5 below half HP and by another 5 below 10% of maximum HP.

details.label: Limits
details.value: A fainted Pokémon or one with a higher level than the Trainer cannot be caught with a Pokéball.

items.name: Pokéball Variants
items.description: Pokéball variants alter a capture attempt or provide a benefit to the Pokémon they hold.

details.label: Capture modifiers
details.value: Great and Ultra Balls lower capture DC; specialized Balls apply their bonus in matching circumstances.

details.label: Master Ball
details.value: The capture attempt succeeds automatically.

details.label: Failed attempt
details.value: A Pokéball is destroyed when its capture attempt fails.

details.label: Held Pokémon
details.value: Some Balls provide rest or hit-die benefits to the Pokémon residing in them.

items.name: Reaching 0 HP
items.description: The outcome for a Pokémon at 0 HP depends on the battle and whether it is stabilized.

details.label: Sanctioned battle
details.value: All damage is non-lethal; a downed Pokémon does not make death saving throws.

details.label: Other battles
details.value: A downed Pokémon makes death saving throws until stabilized.

details.label: Inside a Pokéball
details.value: Death saves are not required; ten uninterrupted minutes inside stabilizes the Pokémon at 0 HP.

details.label: Trainer reaction
details.value: The Trainer may recall the Pokémon and send out another one immediately.

items.name: Healing and Resting
items.description: Pokécenters, rests, and items are the main ways to restore a Pokémon.

details.label: Pokécenter
details.value: Restores HP and cures statuses in under 30 minutes, but does not restore PP or hit dice.

details.label: Short rest
details.value: May take 30 minutes and restores HP by normal 5e rules; it restores neither PP nor a fainted Pokémon.

details.label: Long rest
details.value: Takes at least eight hours and restores HP, statuses, and PP.

details.label: Items and food
details.value: May restore HP, PP, or cure status when given as an action or, where allowed, consumed as a reaction.

items.name: Pokémon Leveling
items.description: Groups may use experience, milestones, or Trainer-matched levels for Pokémon progression.

details.label: HP
details.value: On each level, gain HP from a hit-die roll plus Constitution modifier.

details.label: Moves
details.value: A Pokémon knows at most four Moves; new Move choices occur at levels 2, 6, 10, 14, and 18.

details.label: Ability scores
details.value: Ability Score Improvements occur at levels 4, 8, 12, and 16.

details.label: Damage
details.value: Damaging Moves increase at levels 5, 10, and 17 when their description provides an increase.

items.name: Pokémon Evolution
items.description: A Pokémon may evolve after meeting the condition shown in its stat block.

details.label: Benefits
details.value: Evolution grants the listed ability-score points, double the Pokémon's level as an HP bonus, and the evolved form's core statistics.

details.label: Moves
details.value: Known Moves remain, but future Move choices use only the evolved form's Move list.

details.label: Timing
details.value: Evolution may be delayed, but after declining it the Pokémon must gain another level before evolving.

items.name: Mega Evolution
items.description: A final-stage Pokémon can temporarily exceed its normal limits through Mega Evolution.

details.label: Requirements
details.value: Final evolutionary stage, at least level 10, a Megalite, and a Trainer with a Key Stone.

details.label: Benefits
details.value: AC increases by 2 and ability modifiers are doubled for attack, damage, saving throws, and save DCs.

details.label: Ends
details.value: Ends after combat, after ten minutes outside combat, when the Pokémon faints, or when the Trainer loses the Key Stone.

items.name: Z-Moves and Dynamax
items.description: Z-Power and Dynamax offer powerful temporary options with different equipment and level requirements.

details.label: Z-Move
details.value: Requires level 6, a matching Z-Crystal, and a Trainer with a Z-Ring; it empowers one matching known Move.

details.label: Dynamax
details.value: Requires level 10, adequate space, and a Dynamax Band; it grants temporary HP equal to current HP and Gargantuan size.

details.label: Frequency
details.value: A Pokémon can undergo only one transformation per long rest; a Trainer can induce each transformation kind once per long rest.

items.name: Terastallization
items.description: Terastallization changes a Pokémon's active type to its Tera Type for a short time.

details.label: Requirements
details.value: The Pokémon must be at least level 6 and its Trainer must possess a Tera Orb.

details.label: Type and STAB
details.value: Its type becomes its Tera Type while retaining original STAB; matching Tera Type doubles that STAB bonus.

details.label: Ends
details.value: Ends after combat, after one minute outside combat, when the Pokémon faints, or when the Trainer loses the Tera Orb.

items.name: Harsh Sunlight
items.description: Harsh sunlight amplifies Fire-type Moves and weakens Water-type Moves.

details.label: Fire Moves
details.value: Damage rolls have advantage.

details.label: Water Moves
details.value: Damage rolls have disadvantage.

items.name: Rain
items.description: Rain amplifies Water-type Moves and weakens Fire-type Moves.

details.label: Water Moves
details.value: Damage rolls have advantage.

details.label: Fire Moves
details.value: Damage rolls have disadvantage.

items.name: Sandstorm
items.description: A sandstorm obscures the battlefield and can damage creatures over time.

details.label: Visibility
details.value: The area is lightly obscured.

details.label: Rock-type Pokémon
details.value: Gain +1 AC.

details.label: Move-created storm
details.value: Deals Rock-type damage each turn equal to half the triggering Pokémon's level.

items.name: Hail and Snow
items.description: Icy weather can inflict cold damage or strengthen Ice-type Pokémon defenses.

details.label: Hail
details.value: When created by a Pokémon, it deals Ice-type damage each turn equal to half that Pokémon's level.

details.label: Snow
details.value: Ice-type Pokémon gain +1 AC; a Move may provide a higher bonus.

items.name: Fog
items.description: Fog sharply restricts visibility across the battlefield.

details.label: Visibility
details.value: The area is heavily obscured.

items.name: Electric Terrain
items.description: Electric Terrain empowers Electric-type Moves and protects grounded creatures from sleep.

details.label: Damage
details.value: A creature may double its Move modifier on Electric-type Move damage rolls made inside the terrain.

details.label: Grounded creatures
details.value: Cannot become Asleep.

details.label: Typical extent
details.value: 40-foot radius for 3 rounds when created by a Move.

items.name: Grassy Terrain
items.description: Grassy Terrain empowers Grass-type Moves and heals grounded creatures.

details.label: Damage
details.value: A creature may double its Move modifier on Grass-type Move damage rolls made inside the terrain.

details.label: Grounded creatures
details.value: Recover HP equal to their Proficiency bonus when ending a turn in the terrain.

details.label: Typical extent
details.value: 40-foot radius for 3 rounds when created by a Move.

items.name: Misty Terrain
items.description: Misty Terrain protects grounded creatures from Dragon-type damage and new status conditions.

details.label: Dragon damage
details.value: Grounded creatures are resistant to Dragon-type damage; a vulnerability becomes normal damage instead.

details.label: Grounded creatures
details.value: Cannot gain new status conditions.

details.label: Typical extent
details.value: 60-foot radius for 3 rounds when created by a Move.

items.name: Psychic Terrain
items.description: Psychic Terrain empowers Psychic-type Moves but restricts grounded creatures.

details.label: Damage
details.value: A creature may double its Move modifier on Psychic-type Move damage rolls made inside the terrain.

details.label: Grounded creatures
details.value: Cannot use bonus actions.

details.label: Typical extent
details.value: 40-foot radius for 3 rounds when created by a Move.

items.name: Wild Pokémon Encounters
items.description: Wild encounters support exploration, capture, and battle without requiring every foe to match party strength.

details.label: Levels
details.value: Mix lower and higher levels in groups; use levels rather than Species Rating as the primary difficulty guide.

details.label: Intent
details.value: Use several lower-level Pokémon for capture expeditions and stronger Pokémon for battle-focused encounters.

details.label: Habitats
details.value: Use the biomes listed on Pokémon stat blocks to ground encounters in the current Location.

items.name: Trainer Battles
items.description: Trainer encounters use deliberate Pokémon teams and agreed battle rules.

details.label: Opposing teams
details.value: Trainer Pokémon may use feats, specialization benefits, TM Moves, and stronger statistics.

details.label: Battle terms
details.value: Set the format and item rules before play; opposing Trainer Pokémon cannot be caught.

details.label: Trainer safety
details.value: Sanctioned Trainer battles do not permit Trainers to fight or target other Trainers directly.

items.name: Gym Battles
items.description: Gym Battles are official high-stakes Trainer challenges that should keep the full table involved.

details.label: Theme
details.value: Gym Leaders commonly build teams around a Pokémon type or a clear theme.

details.label: Formats
details.value: Use teamed doubles, full-team battles, or parallel one-on-ones according to the group and encounter goal.

details.label: Rewards
details.value: A victory can grant a Badge, a monetary or TM reward, and experience for defeated Pokémon.

items.name: Damage Type Fundamentals
items.description: Pokémon 5e uses Pokémon damage types in place of the standard D&D damage types.

details.label: Resistance
details.value: A resistant Pokémon takes half damage.

details.label: Vulnerability
details.value: A vulnerable Pokémon takes double damage.

details.label: Dual types
details.value: Dual types do not create double resistance or double vulnerability.

details.label: Order
details.value: Apply resistance or vulnerability after all other damage effects.

items.name: Damage Type Immunity
items.description: Immunity prevents damage and damage-linked secondary effects, not every effect of a Move.

details.label: Damaging Moves
details.value: An immune Pokémon takes no damage and ignores secondary effects tied to the damage.

details.label: Non-damaging Moves
details.value: A non-damaging Move of the same type may still affect the Pokémon.

details.label: Magical physical damage
details.value: Magical bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing damage bypasses an immunity to those D&D damage types.

items.name: Changing a Pokémon's Type
items.description: A changed type updates a Pokémon's matchup profile and STAB calculation.

details.label: Defenses
details.value: Resistances, vulnerabilities, and immunities become those of the new type.

details.label: STAB
details.value: Calculate STAB from the new type.

details.label: Duration
details.value: A temporary change without a stated duration normally ends after a long rest.

items.name: Trainer Class Core Traits
items.description: Every player character uses the Trainer class, whose primary ability is Charisma.

details.label: Hit Points
details.value: Use a d6 per Trainer level; at level 1, HP is 6 + Constitution modifier.

details.label: Saving throw
details.value: Trainers are proficient in Charisma saving throws.

details.label: Skills
details.value: Gain Animal Handling and choose two additional skills from the Trainer list.

details.label: Tools
details.value: Trainers are proficient with Poké Balls, but not armor or weapons.

items.name: Trainer Starting Kit
items.description: A new Trainer starts with the equipment and authorization needed to begin a Pokémon journey.

details.label: Equipment
details.value: Start with 5 Poké Balls, 1 Potion, a Trainer License, and a Pokédex.

details.label: Starter
details.value: Choose one unevolved Pokémon of SR 1/2 or lower, with a chosen nature and non-hidden Ability.

details.label: Funds
details.value: Start with ₽1,000 plus ₽100 × 4d4.

details.label: License
details.value: A license authorizes captures and access to selected Pokécenter and Poké Mart services.

items.name: Trainer Class Milestones
items.description: Trainer features arrive at specific levels, expanding Pokémon capacity, control, and personal expertise.

details.label: Level 1
details.value: Gain a Starter Pokémon and a Specialization.

details.label: Level 2
details.value: Choose a Trainer Path; Path features follow at levels 5, 9, and 15.

details.label: Growth
details.value: Gain Control Upgrades at levels 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, and 17, and Ability Score Improvements at 4, 8, 12, and 16.

details.label: Pokéslots
details.value: Carry 3 Pokémon at level 1, then gain one additional slot at levels 5, 10, and 15.

details.label: High levels
details.value: Gain Trainer's Resolve at 10, Pokémon Tracker at 13, an Epic Boon at 19, and Master Trainer at 20.

items.name: Trainer Leveling Methods
items.description: The Game Master can tie Trainer progression to Pokémon levels, story milestones, or Pokédex discoveries.

details.label: Pokémon levels
details.value: Use the total level of the Trainer's highest-level Pokémon, up to their current Pokéslot count.

details.label: Milestones
details.value: Advance the group after major story achievements, such as earning a Gym Badge.

details.label: Pokédex entries
details.value: Use the number of registered Pokémon to reward discovery-focused play.

details.label: Level-up benefit
details.value: On every Trainer level, gain HP from a hit-die roll plus Constitution modifier; higher Constitution applies retroactively.

items.name: Trainer Paths
items.description: At level 2, a Trainer chooses a Path that expresses their long-term goal and grants features through level 15.

details.label: Feature levels
details.value: A Path grants its first feature at level 2, then additional features at levels 5, 9, and 15.

details.label: Examples
details.value: Ace Trainer, Researcher, Nurse, Type Master, Ranger, Tactician, and Pokémon Collector are core Paths.

details.label: Supplements
details.value: Commander and Pokémon Breeder use the Bonds and Breeding supplements respectively.

items.name: Bond Levels
items.description: The Bond Level describes the evolving relationship between a Pokémon and its Trainer.

details.label: Range
details.value: Bond Levels range from -3 to +3 and may affect obedience, evolution, and Bond Points.

details.label: Starting bond
details.value: Most newly caught Pokémon begin at +0 or lower; they rarely begin above +1.

details.label: Narrative decision
details.value: The Trainer and Game Master agree when a Bond Level changes.

details.label: Examples
details.value: Time together, favored food, and difficult victories may raise a bond; neglect or cruel treatment may lower it.

items.name: Bond Points
items.description: Pokémon with a positive Bond Level receive Bond Points equal to that level.

details.label: Points
details.value: At Bond Level +1, +2, or +3, a Pokémon has 1, 2, or 3 Bond Points respectively.

details.label: Recovery
details.value: All spent Bond Points return at the end of a long rest.

details.label: Advantage
details.value: Spend 1 Bond Point after rolling a d20 ability check, attack roll, or saving throw to gain advantage.

details.label: Protection
details.value: Spend 1 Bond Point when a creature attacks the Pokémon to impose disadvantage on that attack roll.

items.name: Negative Bond Levels
items.description: A negative Bond Level reflects an upset, indifferent, or disloyal Pokémon.

details.label: Level -1
details.value: An upset Pokémon holds a grudge that affects it in battle.

details.label: Level -2
details.value: When commanded, roll a d20. On 10 or lower, the Pokémon hesitates and follows the command with disadvantage.

details.label: Level -3
details.value: When commanded, roll a d20. On 10 or lower, the Pokémon disobeys by doing nothing or acting on its own.

items.name: Pokémon Eggs and Breeding
items.description: At the end of an in-game day, eligible Pokémon may attempt to create an egg.

details.label: Trainer relationship
details.value: The Pokémon must share a Trainer, or their Trainers must be in the same party.

details.label: Bond
details.value: Each parent needs Bond Level +2 or higher.

details.label: Compatibility
details.value: The parents need opposite genders and a shared Egg Group; Undiscovered Pokémon cannot breed.

details.label: Pokéslot
details.value: The Trainer needs an open Pokéslot for the egg.

details.label: Breeding check
details.value: Roll a straight d20 against a DC set by the parents' combined Bond Levels.

items.name: Egg Incubation
items.description: A new egg receives a Hatch Time counter based on the Pokémon's Species Rating.

details.label: Progress
details.value: At the start of each in-game day or session, roll 1d100 + 50 and reduce the remaining counter by the result.

details.label: Care
details.value: Progress is possible only when the Trainer carried the egg through the night or much of the previous session.

details.label: Fragility
details.value: An egg has AC 8 and 10 HP; at 0 HP it breaks and the Pokémon inside is lost.

details.label: Incubators
details.value: Basic, Plus, and Super Incubators reduce Hatch Time by an additional 1d20, 2d20, or 3d20 per day.

items.name: Hatching a Pokémon
items.description: When Hatch Time reaches 0, determine the hatched Pokémon's initial species, traits, Moves, and bond.

details.label: Species
details.value: Use the female parent's lowest evolutionary form at its minimum found level.

details.label: Nature and gender
details.value: Roll a d100 on the Nature table and against the species' Gender Rate.

details.label: Moves
details.value: Choose starting Moves and add eligible Egg Moves or shared parent Moves as described by the breeding rules.

details.label: Ability
details.value: Flip a coin: heads inherits the female parent's Ability; tails selects randomly from the hatched Pokémon's stat block.

details.label: Bond
details.value: The hatchling begins at Bond Level +1, or +2 if it spent the full incubation period in the Trainer's party.

items.name: Breeding Special Cases
items.description: Some Egg Groups and species follow special rules when breeding.

details.label: Ditto
details.value: Ditto can breed with any Pokémon regardless of gender or Egg Group; the non-Ditto parent determines the hatched species.

details.label: Undiscovered
details.value: Baby and Legendary Pokémon in the Undiscovered Egg Group cannot breed.

details.label: Gendered species
details.value: Species with separate gender stat blocks may produce either species; use the hatchling's Gender Rate to decide.

items.name: Legendary Boss Battles
items.description: The Game Master can give a major enemy Legendary Abilities to make a boss encounter more dangerous and memorable.

details.label: Purpose
details.value: Use these abilities for unusually difficult enemies, such as a dangerous wild threat or a Legendary Pokémon.

details.label: Selection
details.value: Choose abilities that reinforce the boss's narrative role and intended battlefield behavior.

details.label: Reward
details.value: Consider awarding additional experience for defeating a creature with one or more Legendary Abilities.

items.name: Legendary Defensive Abilities
items.description: Defensive Legendary Abilities help a boss endure decisive player turns.

details.label: Legendary Grit
details.value: A limited number of times per day, the Pokémon can turn a failed saving throw into a success.

details.label: Legendary Resistance
details.value: A limited number of times per day, the Pokémon can halve damage from a Move.

details.label: Legendary Resilience
details.value: The Pokémon can sacrifice its action to remove a negative status effect from itself.

details.label: Legendary Armor
details.value: As a reaction a limited number of times per day, the Pokémon can increase AC enough to turn an attack into a miss.

details.label: Legendary Toughness
details.value: Base HP on the maximum hit-die roll for every level.

items.name: Legendary Offense and Energy
items.description: Offensive and energy abilities let a boss create sustained pressure in battle.

details.label: Legendary Attack I
details.value: Trade the current action for two attacks next turn, or make two attacks now and sacrifice the next action.

details.label: Legendary Attack II
details.value: Make two attacks on each turn.

details.label: Legendary Attack III
details.value: Use a signature Move twice in one turn.

details.label: Legendary Energy I
details.value: Sacrifice an action to restore all PP for one Move.

details.label: Legendary Energy II
details.value: Every Move has double its normal PP.

items.name: Legendary Mobility and Utility
items.description: Mobility and utility abilities make a boss harder to contain and more tactically flexible.

details.label: Legendary Nimbleness
details.value: Move up to speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

details.label: Legendary Speed
details.value: A limited number of times per day, double movement.

details.label: Legendary Reflexes
details.value: Use two reactions in a combat round.

details.label: Legendary Knowledge
details.value: Choose Moves from anywhere in the Pokémon's Move list regardless of level.
